'''Barbara Wayne Abraham-Shrauner''' is an American physicist, applied mathematician, and electrical engineer. She was known for her research on [[magnetohydrodynamics]] and [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] phenomena, including mathematical modeling of shocks and [[Alfvén waves]], observation of the [[solar wind]], and applications to the [[plasma etching]] of [[semiconductor]]s,{{r|faps|burlaga}} as well as on hidden symmetries and nonlocal symmetries in [[differential equation]]s.{{r|sym}} She is retired as a professor of electrical and systems engineering at the [[McKelvey School of Engineering]] at [[Washington University in St. Louis]].{{r|wustl}}

==Education and career==
Abraham-Shrauner graduated from Madison High School in 1952. She earned her bachelor's degree from the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] in 1956.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barbara Shrauner |url=https://engineering.washu.edu/faculty/Barbara-Shrauner.html |access-date=2025-05-08 |website=[[McKelvey School of Engineering]] |language=en}}</ref>
She earned a master's degree  from [[Harvard University]] in 1957 and completed her Ph.D. there in 1962.{{r|wustl}}

She joined Washington University in St. Louis faculty in 1966, after postdoctoral research at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] and [[NASA]] [[Ames Research Center]], and retired from full-time service in 2003 at Washington University, where she continues to hold an affiliation as a part-time Senior Professor in the Department of Electrical and Systems Engineering.{{r|wustl}}

==Recognition==
Abraham-Shrauner was named a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS) in 1999, after a nomination from the APS Division of Plasma Physics, "for important theoretical contributions to a broad range of plasma topics, including: space plasmas, nonlinear dynamics, and plasma processing".{{r|faps}} She is a part of the Barbara Abraham Shrauner Endowed Scholarship in Physics to award undergraduate students that are involved in pursuing Physics or Engineering Physics.

==Personal life==
Abraham-Shrauner was married to James Ely Shrauner (1933–2015), a professor of physics in [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis]].{{r|jes}}<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lutz |first=Diana |date=June 4, 2015 |title=Obituary: James 'Ely' Shrauner, professor emeritus of physics, 82 |url=https://source.washu.edu/2015/06/obituary-james-ely-shraunerprofessor-emeritus-of-physics-82/ |access-date= |website=The Source |language=en-US}}</ref>
